subject: [Incident] Throughput drop on reserved cluster — impact details and next steps
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya@atlasretail.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Severe throughput drop on reserved cluster - urgent

Hi Marissa,

We observed a sharp throughput drop starting ~07:48 PDT on our reserved GPU cluster (cluster-id: atl-prod-1). Token throughput fell ~70% for 30+ minutes and several tail requests timed out. We attached the client-side traces and a short support log excerpt. Our production flows have degraded impact on user experience.

What we're seeing:
- Spike in request latency from 120ms median to 1.8s
- Queue depth increased and several requests saw 503s
- No change on our side (no rollout) — we rely on your reserved capacity SLA

Can you confirm what happened and when we can expect full recovery? This is customer-facing and time-sensitive.

Attachments: throughput_trace_0915.log, support_log_0915.txt

Thanks,
Priya Shah

Subject: Re: Severe throughput drop on reserved cluster - urgent

Update from triage (summary):

What we found so far:
- Root cause: transient imbalance between node headroom and autoscaler decisions during a short burst of long-context generation; autoscaler inhibited scale-out due to conservative eviction thresholds. That produced a short-lived queueing chokepoint on a subset of nodes (atl-prod-1).
- Evidence: KV cache growth correlated with spike windows in throughput_trace_0915.log; increased gRPC queue depth and headroom signals on 3/16 nodes.

Immediate mitigations applied (15:10 PDT):
1) Overrode autoscale policy for atl-prod-1 to force an immediate +30% capacity increase (temporary policy).
2) Bounced 2 serving pools to rebalance cached KV shards and reduce eviction thrash.
3) Enabled an elevated short-window fallback to our warm-standby nodes for high-latency requests.

Customer impact and timeline:
- Throughput and latencies returned to normal within ~18 minutes of intervention.
- We'll keep the autoscale override in place for 2 hours while we validate stability, then revert with a conservative warmup.

Follow-ups planned:
- Postmortem write-up with timeline, root cause, and permanent mitigations (expected within 5 business days).
- Suggestion: change autoscaler policy defaults for reserved clusters with long-context workloads and expose a config knob for customers to opt into prefix cache-aware scaling.

I will attach the filtered diagnostic logs to the ticket.

— Karthik (on-call, Platform Ops)

- 07:48 PDT: elevated request latency first observed by Atlas.
- 07:50–08:06 PDT: autoscaler did not scale (inhibited by eviction thresholds).
- 08:06–08:24 PDT: mitigation actions executed (autoscale override + pool bounce); normal throughput restored ~08:24 PDT.

Postmortem and permanent mitigations:
- We are preparing a formal postmortem with full timeline, logs, and proposed permanent fixes. Expect delivery by EOD Wed, 2026-09-23.
- Permanent mitigations under consideration: cache-aware autoscaler tuning, a reserved-cluster warm-standby policy, and an opt-in safety override for long-context workloads.

Credits and billing:

For transparency, we provisionally propose a pro-rated credit equivalent to 4 hours of reserved throughput for the affected cluster while we finalize the exact number. Stephanie will open the billing ticket and send a DocuSign link if needed.
